Epitome

ih-PIT-uh-mee -- FOUR syllables, stress on the second syllable, PIT. The ending is 'mee': never say 'EP-ih-tohm.' · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Epitome is a perfect example or embodiment of a quality.

With every tiny tool hung in its outlined place, the watchmaker's bench is the epitome of order.

Worked Example

Two hundred meters from the finish, the race leader hears a crash behind her -- her closest rival has fallen hard. She stops, runs BACK, and half-carries the injured girl across the line before crossing it herself, in last place. The next morning, every headline calls her the epitome of sportsmanship.

The runner is the epitome of sportsmanship: the quality itself, embodied at its absolute best. That is what epitome does -- it points at one person or thing and says: if you want to see this quality perfectly displayed, look HERE. The pattern is always 'the epitome OF' plus the quality.

How Epitome Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

embodiment

embodiment: a quality given concrete, living form

essence

essence: the purest core of something

personification

personification: a quality so perfectly shown in a person that they seem to BE it

Antonyms

opposite

opposite: something completely contrary to a quality

worst example

worst example: a case that shows a quality at its weakest

How Strong Is It? — embodiment → epitome → personification

embodiment vs. epitome

embodiment vs. epitome: Embodiment says a quality has taken concrete form -- the statue is an embodiment of hope -- without ranking how well.

personification vs. epitome

personification vs. epitome: Personification is the strongest: an embodiment gives the quality A form, but calling someone the personification of patience says the quality and the person have become impossible to tell apart.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of epitome.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — epi-

prefix — epi-: into, upon (Greek)

root — tome

root — tome: to cut (Greek temnein 'to cut')

Put it together

Put it together: Epitome is Greek for 'a cutting into' -- epi- plus temnein, 'to cut.' It first meant a SUMMARY: a long book cut down to its essentials. From there the meaning slid from the perfect condensation of a book to the perfect condensation of a quality: the epitome of grace is grace with everything inessential cut away, leaving only the quality itself, concentrated in one example.

Use the root in a new word: atom

Use the root in a new word: atom: Ancient Greek thinkers named the atom for the particle they believed could not be cut any smaller.

Root Check

Word Choice

Epitome travels in one pattern: THE EPITOME OF plus a quality -- the epitome of grace, of luxury, of tact. Keep it apart from its unit-mate archetype: the epitome is the finest EMBODIMENT of a quality, while the archetype is the ORIGINAL PATTERN later examples are modeled on. A hotel can be the epitome of luxury without any other hotel copying it; Sherlock Holmes is the archetype of the detective because every later sleuth descends from him. And mind the pronunciation: ih-PIT-uh-mee.
